newsitem.title: USA: General Dynamics bid for United Defense questioned.
newsitem.headline: General Dynamics bid for United Defense questioned.

text.p: U.S. Sen. Arlen Specter said on Friday he had asked the Justice Department to examine the antitrust implications raised by General Dynamics Corp's bid for military vehicle producer United Defense LP.

"I believe the antitrust implications of such an acquisition raise concerns and deserve close scrutiny by your agency and the appropriate congressional oversight committees," Specter said in a letter to Assistant Attorney General Joel Klein, who heads Justice's Antitrust Division.
Specter said General Dynamics and United Defense were currently the only U.S. companies making armored vehicles, compared with five companies in that business four years ago,
Specter sits on the Senate Appropriations Committee's defense subcommittee and the Senate Judiciary Committee's antitrust subcommittee.
United Defense is 60 percent owned by FMC Corp and 40 percent owned by Harsco Corp.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that other companies interested in United Defense include the closely held Carlyle Group and Alliant Techsystems Inc.
